accroche: For forty years, England's oldest human ancestor was an ape's jaw, filed down and stained.
contenu_vulgarise:
On December 18, 1912, before the Geological Society of London, the paleontologist Arthur Smith Woodward presents a skull reconstruction that will, for forty years, bear the name Piltdown Man. The amateur Charles Dawson claims to have found it in a gravel pit in Sussex: a braincase with a human look, paired with a jaw with an apelike look. The missing link between ape and man, found in England.

## A forgery that holds for forty years

The affair holds together because it flatters an expectation: in the early twentieth century, several British scholars hope that the cradle of humanity lies in Europe. Piltdown's large skull and apelike jaw fit the idea that a large brain preceded the modern jaw in human evolution, an order that other fossils, found elsewhere, already contradicted.

Doubts exist as early as the 1910s, but nothing settles them before chemistry does. In 1949, the geologist Kenneth Oakley applies to the bone and the tooth a still-recent method: fluorine dating, since fluorine accumulates in fossil bone through contact with the soil over millennia. First troubling result: the jaw appears markedly younger than the skull.

## The chemical proof

In 1953, Oakley resumes the analysis with Joseph Weiner and Wilfrid Le Gros Clark, on finer samples. The figures, published on November 21, 1953 in the Bulletin of the British Museum (Natural History), leave no room for doubt: the skull contains 0.1% fluorine, a level expected of an Upper Pleistocene bone, while the jaw and tooth cap out below 0.04%, the level of a recent tooth. Under the microscope, the molars show regular scratches, the mark of a file, and beneath the brown iron staining that imitated the local gravel's patina, the dentine of a canine had remained as white as that of a present-day tooth.

The verdict: a modern human skull paired with a jaw and teeth from an orangutan, filed down and then stained to imitate a fossil. Forty-one years separate the 1912 presentation from its refutation.

## What this shifts

It was not observation that ended the affair: generations of scholars had looked at the same bones without seeing the forgery, partly because they were hoping for exactly what those bones seemed to confirm. It was a chemical measurement, indifferent to what one hoped to find, that settled it. The history of science often remembers fraud as a failure of the discipline. Piltdown is also the opposite: proof that a method, once refined, eventually catches up with what the eye, loaded with expectation, had let through for forty-one years.

repere.texte: Piltdown's skull contained 0.1% fluorine, a level expected of an Upper Pleistocene bone. The jaw and tooth, meanwhile, capped out below 0.04%, the level of a recent tooth.
repere.source: Weiner, Oakley & Le Gros Clark, Bulletin of the British Museum (Natural History), Geology, vol. 2, no. 3, 1953

carte.punch: England's oldest prehistoric ancestor was a forgery made in a workshop.
carte.idee: Presented in 1912 as the missing link in human evolution, Piltdown Man was a modern human skull paired with a filed and stained orangutan jaw. A measurement of the bone's fluorine content unmasked the fraud, forty-one years later, in 1953.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The museum's collection and the full history of the discovery through to its unraveling.

quiz.question: What made it possible, in 1953, to prove that Piltdown Man was a forgery?
choix: A witness confessed forty years later to having fabricated the fossil
A new chemical measurement, the fluorine content of the bone, showed that the jaw was far more recent than the skull
A new fossil found elsewhere made the Piltdown remains incompatible with the rest of the evidence
Visual examination of the bones by new paleontologists was enough to spot the artificial staining
quiz.explication: Fluorine dating, refined in 1953, revealed that the jaw and tooth contained far less fluorine than the skull, and so were much younger: no confession or new discovery elsewhere was needed, a chemical measurement alone settled it.
